MNQ Entry Shootout

Which confirmation is worth waiting for: the ORB break, VWAP, a 5-minute FVG, or a mix? Every entry runs through the same 480 risk-management settings, buys and sells apart. Each rule is picked on 2020–2023 and judged on 2024–2026, which it never saw. A random-side benchmark shows how much of each result is just MNQ going up.

The short answer

Which entry is worth waiting for

For each entry and side, the best rule of 2020–23 (net ÷ drawdown, at least 150 trades a side), then what that same rule did in 2024–26. "Rules up" = the share of all 480 settings that made money in 2024–26. Click a row to see its curve and years below.

Typical result, not just the best one

The median 2024–26 result per trade (in R) across all 480 settings of each entry. A best pick can be luck; the median shows whether the entry itself carries anything.

Every rule

How it was tested

A break or cross is a 5-minute close (candles from 09:30 New York). Market entries fill at the next minute's open plus 1 tick. FVG entries are limits at the gap's near edge that fill only when price trades 1 tick through, cancelled on a close beyond the gap's far edge. FVG = candle 1's high below candle 3's low (buy), or the other way (sell). The VWAP is the session VWAP from 09:30. One trade a day. Costs $1.74 a round trip plus 1 tick on every stop. A minute that touches both the stop and the target counts as the stop. "ORB + VWAP" turned out identical to "ORB only": once a 5-minute candle closes beyond the opening range, price is already on that side of the VWAP. The random-side benchmark enters at the same minute as the ORB break but flips a coin for the direction.
